Surgical Breast Enlargement

Recovery After a Breast Lift

Recovery varies with the extent of the lift and whether it is combined with other surgery. Your surgeon’s instructions take priority.

Home/Surgical Breast Enlargement/Breast lift/Recovery After a Breast Lift

Recovery varies with the extent of the lift and whether it is combined with other surgery. Your surgeon’s instructions take priority over any general timeline.

The first days

  • Soreness, swelling, bruising and tightness
  • Dressings and a surgical or support bra
  • Sometimes small drains, removed after a few days
  • Numbness or altered sensation around the breast and nipple

Most people go home the same day or after one night.

Pain and medicines

You will usually be given pain relief. Follow instructions and avoid medicines you were told to stop, since some raise bleeding risk.

Activity

  • Walk gently from early on, which helps circulation
  • Avoid lifting, pushing and strenuous exercise for several weeks, as advised
  • Avoid raising your arms above shoulder height if told to, since tension can stress wounds
  • Return to desk work after a period determined by your surgeon, and to heavier work later

Sleeping

Sleeping on your back with your upper body slightly raised is commonly advised. Avoid sleeping on your front.

Support garments

Wear the recommended bra as directed, usually for several weeks. Avoid underwired bras until your surgeon says it is safe.

Wound and scar care

Keep dressings clean and dry as instructed, and attend wound checks. Scars mature over a year or more. Protect them from the sun.

The shape will change

Swelling and tightness mean the breasts may look high and tight at first. They settle gradually over weeks to months.

Follow-up is part of recovery

Attend wound and scar checks even if you feel well. Ask when changes in shape, nipple sensation or scar colour are expected and when they are not. Take concerns to your own surgical team rather than changing dressings, bras or scar treatments based only on advice online.

Driving and work

Do not drive while taking strong pain relief or while movement is restricted. Desk work may be possible after a week or two, but physical work and exercise usually need longer. Ask for advice specific to your operation.

When swelling settles

Early swelling can make the breasts look high and tight. Most change occurs over the first few months, but subtle settling can continue for longer. Avoid judging the final shape in the first weeks.

Call your surgeon if you notice

Fever, increasing pain, spreading redness, a wound opening, rapid swelling on one side, or skin around the nipple turning dark or pale. See warning signs.

Key takeaway

Plan for rest, help at home and patience while the shape settles. See Breast Lift Surgery.
